articles.content:
Sponsored by Bitwarden: The Open Source Password Manager that keeps your passwords secure and accessible across all your devices. Visit https://bitwarden.com/tux to get started.

This episode is going to be so packed full of great stuff that it’s kind of ridiculous!

KDE is celebrating 30 years of the project, with Plasma 6.8, bringing some exciting improvements and a major change to the Linux desktop.

Meanwhile, Fortnite is finally coming to Linux, and some distributions are already making preparations to get it working.

Linux 7.3 is here with improvements for gaming, hardware, and performance, plus a few unexpected additions.

And Ubuntu 26.10 has arrived, but Canonical has even bigger plans that could change the future of Ubuntu Desktop.

All of that and more! So let's jump into Your Source for Linux GNews and see what's happened This Week in Linux.

articles.title: 30 Years of KDE: Inside Plasma 6.8, Wayland Switch, & more with Nate Graham & Aleix Pol
articles.author: Michael Tunnell
articles.summary: KDE is celebrating its 30th anniversary, Plasma 6.8 is right around the corner, and Akademy is bringing the KDE community together once again. I sat down with KDE’s Nate Graham and Aleix Pol to talk about Plasma 6.8, the move to Wayland, what happens behind the scenes at Akademy, how KDE has evolved
articles.content:
KDE is celebrating its 30th anniversary, Plasma 6.8 is right around the corner, and Akademy is bringing the KDE community together once again.

I sat down with KDE’s Nate Graham and Aleix Pol to talk about Plasma 6.8, the move to Wayland, what happens behind the scenes at Akademy, how KDE has evolved over the past three decades, and what the future could look like for one of Linux’s biggest desktop projects.

Asahi Linux pulled off another major Apple Silicon milestone with M3 Macs. Valve is building one of the wildest compatibility stacks we've seen yet for the Steam Frame.
